content: Deglycyrrhizinated licorice, commonly abbreviated as DGL, is a form of licorice from which the compound glycyrrhizin has been removed. It is primarily used as an herbal supplement for the treatment of gastric and duodenal ulcers. The standard recommended dosage of DGL is 760 mg, which should be chewed approximately 20 minutes before a meal. Clinical studies conducted on both humans and animals have demonstrated that DGL significantly reduces the size of gastric ulcers and accelerates the healing process. In one study, 44% of participants experienced complete healing of their ulcers, compared to only 6% in the placebo group. DGL has also been shown to be effective in treating duodenal ulcers. In a specific study involving 40 patients who had suffered from duodenal ulcers for 4 to 12 years, participants were treated with either 3 grams of DGL daily for 8 weeks or 4.5 grams daily for 12 weeks. All patients exhibited significant improvement, with the higher dosage yielding the most pronounced results. Another study has indicated that the therapeutic effects of DGL are comparable to those of cimetidine, a commonly used medication for ulcers. Importantly, there have been no documented cases of DGL overdose, and reported side effects are minimal, with occasional instances of nausea and diarrhea. Furthermore, DGL does not appear to interact with other medications used to treat ulcers. In certain regions, such as Europe, South Africa, and Canada, DGL is available in a medicinal preparation known as Caved-S. In the United States, it is marketed as an herbal supplement. Additionally, DGL has been reported to be beneficial in the treatment of aphthous ulcers, commonly referred to as canker sores.
